title: CodeCharta cc.json 2.0
description: The cc.json 2.0 wire format: { meta, files, lenses }. `files` is the identity layer (one root folder, nested children, each node carrying a stable id); `lenses` are additive analysis overlays joined to files by id. This is the analysis-side format `ccsh` emits and `ccsh check` validates. See dev_docs/cc-json-2.0-format.md for the prose spec.

files.description: Exactly one root folder; the identity layer (no metrics on the node).

Meta.description: Project metadata. `checksum` is an MD5 over the serialized files+lenses; `commitHash` is an optional short git SHA.

apiVersion.description: Major must be 2; any minor. Minors are additive-only (new optional fields only, never remove/rename/repurpose); a breaking change is a new major. See cc-json-2.0-format.md.

FileNode.description: A file or folder. `id` = first 16 hex of sha-256(canonical tree path). A File may not have children. `contentHash` is the optional per-file xxhash64.

Lenses.description: Additive overlays joined to `files` by id. `metrics`, `dependency` and `clusters` are concrete; `domain`/`security` are reserved; any unknown top-level lens is preserved verbatim on round-trip (hence no additionalProperties:false here).

MetricsLens.description: Per-node metrics, keyed by node id, plus their descriptors and types.

attributes.description: Map of node id -> metric map (numeric or, for e.g. authors, list values).

DependencyLens.description: Edges between nodes (by id) plus the edge attribute types and descriptors.

Edge.description: A dependency edge referencing its endpoints by node id.

ClustersLens.description: Named clusterings of nodes, joined to `files` by id. Structurally a cross-cutting relation like edges, not a per-node metric. Defined but not yet produced or visualized; see dev_docs/cc-json-2.0-clusters-lens.md.

clusterings.description: Map of clustering id -> clustering. A keyed map because clusterings merge by exactly one key, so JSON itself enforces id uniqueness.

Clustering.description: One grouping of the nodes (author ownership, temporal coupling, feature scope, ...). A file may carry several orthogonal clusterings side by side; views activate one at a time, like the edge metric today.

membership.description: How a node may belong to clusters. `partition`: at most one cluster, weight implied 1. `weighted`: overlapping fractional membership; a node's weights across the clusters of this clustering must sum to at most 1 — a semantic invariant that JSON Schema cannot express, so it is not validated here. `overlay`: independent per-cluster membership; weights are per-cluster and never summed across clusters.

weightBasis.description: Names the metrics lens key the member weights are a fraction of (e.g. `rloc`, `loc`, `commits`), so views can weight aggregation with real per-node values.

analyzers.description: The producers that contributed to this clustering; merged by union.

clusters.description: Producer-controlled display order; an array rather than a map because clusters are fuller records.

Cluster.description: A single group of nodes within a clustering, carrying its own attributes (described by the clustering's descriptors and types). `parentId` forms an optional forest within the clustering; flat clusterings leave it null or omit it.

ClusterMember.description: A node's membership in a cluster, referencing the node by id — the same join as edges. `weight` is the fraction of the clustering's `weightBasis` attributed to this cluster; omitted means 1.

AttributeDescriptor.description: Human-facing metadata for a metric/edge attribute.
